resolutions.researcher_notes: Original opec.org ASB2017 link is dead (redirects home). Recovered ASB2012 PDF via Wayback (live 200; url_verifier's raw substring check can't read the PDF text stream -- a documented false-negative for PDFs -- so content was confirmed manually with pdftotext -layout: p.75, Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011', Libya section, row 'Bahr Assalam/Mellitah  Mellitah Oil and Gas  110  36  25,205,324  na' -- listing under the operating-pipelines table supports Status=operating). Second, independent source: offshore-technology.com (GlobalData) describes the Bahr Essalam field's 36in pipeline to Mellitah in ongoing present-tense operational terms, with Phase II first gas achieved July 2018, i.e. an actively producing/operating line as of the article. Two independent origins (OPEC vs GlobalData) -> high.

No source found that states a construction-START year of 2002 specifically for this pipeline segment. OPEC ASB Table 4.10 (2012, 2013/14 editions, both checked via Wayback/pdftotext) has no construction-year column, only owner/length/diameter(/capacity). offshore-technology.com and Wikipedia (National Oil Corporation, Greenstream pipeline, Bouri Field) all give Phase I first-gas/commissioning as 2005 (Western Libyan Gas Project came online Oct 2004, Bahr Essalam gas added 2005) but do not separately date construction start; industry practice for a project like this would put construction ~2-3 years ahead of first gas, consistent with 2002, but I could not find a source that states 2002 explicitly, so leaving UNRESOLVED per standing rule 2 rather than inferring/fabricating a supporting citation.

offshore-technology.com states explicitly: 'Phase I production commenced [in 2005]' and 'Phase II achieved first gas in July 2018' -- exact match to both StartYear1=2005 and StartYear2=2018 (FID for Phase II was 2015, distinct from the 2018 start). Second, independent source for StartYear1: Wikipedia's National Oil Corporation article states Bahr Essalam field gas was added to the Western Libyan Gas Project/Greenstream system in 2005 (WLGP itself came online Oct 2004 from Wafa/Bouri fields; Bahr Essalam joined in 2005). StartYear2=2018 currently rests on the single offshore-technology.com source (no second explicit citation found for the exact 2018 date), but StartYear1=2005 has two independent corroborating sources -> overall high given the primary_value (2005) is doubly corroborated.

FLAGGED VALUE CONTRADICTION: OPEC ASB2012 (Wayback-recovered; opec.org original dead), Table 4.10 p.75, gives capacity for the exact named segment 'Bahr Assalam/Mellitah' as 25,205,324 (in units of 1,000 scm/yr) = ~25.2 bcm/yr -- NOT 28.00 bcm/yr as in the mainsheet. This is the only source found that states a numeric design capacity for this specific pipeline (checked ASB2013/2014 Wayback editions -- their version of Table 4.10 dropped the capacity column entirely for this period, only length+diameter remain; offshore-technology.com gives field PRODUCTION figures -- 600 then +400=1,100 mmscfd post-Phase II, i.e. ~11.3 bcm/yr of gas -- but that is field output, not pipeline design capacity, and does not match 28 either). 25.2 vs 28 bcm/yr is a ~10% gap; plausibly the mainsheet figure reflects a later nameplate/compression upgrade (Phase II, first gas 2018, postdates the 2012 ASB figure) that I could not independently confirm. Citing as the closest available quantitative source with the discrepancy flagged for the mainsheet team to reconcile; tier low, single OPEC-family source, does not exactly support the stated 28.00 value.

Both dead-opec.org PDFs recovered via Wayback (live 200s; content confirmed with pdftotext, not the automated substring screen, which cannot read PDF text streams). ASB2014 (2013 data), Table 4.10 Libya section: 'Bahr es Salam/Mellitah (2)  Mellitah Oil & Gas  2 x 68  10, 36' -- a twin-pipe corridor (10in condensate + 36in gas line), EACH line 68 miles long = 109.4 km, matching LengthKnown=109.00 km almost exactly (and confirming the twin-pipe design independently corroborated by offshore-technology.com's mention of a separate 10in condensate line alongside the 36in gas line). ASB2012 (2011 data) gives '110' for the same segment (header column is mislabeled 'miles' but the Algeria/Libya rows in that edition are inconsistent with true mile conversions elsewhere in the same table, and 110 as km is a near-identical match to 109km, closer than treating it as miles). Both sources are OPEC-family (not independent of each other), but two separate ASB editions corroborate the same ~109km figure -> medium.

offshore-technology.com states verbatim: gas is 'directly pumped and conveyed...to Mellitah' with the field's export line described as 'a 36in-diameter pipeline to the onshore Mellitah plant' -- exact match to Diameter=36.00in. Independently, OPEC ASB2012 (Wayback; content confirmed via pdftotext since the automated substring screen can't parse PDF streams) Table 4.10 p.75 lists 'Bahr Assalam/Mellitah...36' inches diameter, and ASB2014's twin-pipe entry '10, 36' names the 36in line as the gas leg. Two independent origins (GlobalData vs OPEC) both giving 36in -> high.

offshore-technology.com: the Bahr Essalam field sits 'in the Mediterranean Sea approximately 120km northwest of Tripoli, Libya' within Block NC41, with gas piped 'to the onshore Mellitah plant' -- supports StartPrefecture/District=Bahr Assalam, EndLocation=Mellitah, both ends CountryOrArea=Libya. Independently, OPEC ASB2012 (Wayback; pdftotext-confirmed) lists the segment 'Bahr Assalam/Mellitah' by name under the 'Libya' country heading in Table 4.10. Two independent origins -> high. No source gives a Prefecture/Province more granular than 'Libya' for the offshore start point, consistent with the mainsheet leaving that field as the field name itself.

offshore-technology.com: field/pipeline 'is operated by Mellitah Oil & Gas (MOG)'. Also corroborated (OPEC ASB, owner/operator column: 'Mellitah Oil and Gas' / 'Mellitah Oil & Gas'). Arabic name checked against Arabic Wikipedia's article on the company ('حقل مليته للنفط و الغاز'), whose title/body give the Arabic name as 'شركة مليته للنفط والغاز' (Mellitah Oil and Gas Company) -- matches GEM's OperatorLocalLanguage core name 'مليته للنفط و الغاز' closely; GEM's value additionally carries a 'B.V.' suffix ('بي في') not present in the ar.wikipedia text -- likely the Dutch B.V. holding-entity naming convention used for several Libyan JVs; flagging as a minor naming variant, not a mismatch on the operator's identity. Two independent origins (GlobalData + Wikipedia/company sourcing) -> high.

offshore-technology.com states Mellitah Oil & Gas (MOG) 'operates as an equal joint venture between Eni and Libya's National Oil Corporation (NOC), with each holding 50% equity' -- exact match to Owner1=Libyan National Oil Corp 50%, Owner2=Eni SpA 50%. Independently corroborated by Wikipedia's National Oil Corporation article: the Western Libyan Gas Project (which the Bahr Essalam field/pipeline is part of) is 'a 50-50 joint venture between NOC and Eni'. Two independent origins -> high.
